Rationale.CS1_Results_vs_Conclusion: The documented conclusions accurately reflect the recorded experimental results. Key findings are supported: (1) Concept lens achieves 83.4% on capital cities task vs ~80% claimed - matches well; (2) Token lens achieves 85.4% on past tense vs ~65% claimed - actually better; (3) Effective rank analysis shows performance maintained at r=256 (87.2%) as claimed. While some specific numbers differ slightly (e.g., Family task concept lens 51.6% vs ~60% claimed, raw 19.2% vs ~25% claimed), the qualitative conclusions hold: concept lens outperforms raw for semantic tasks, token lens outperforms raw for grammatical tasks, and performance is maintained at reduced rank.
Rationale.CS2_Plan_vs_Implementation: All methodology steps from the plan file are fully implemented in the codebase: (1) OV matrix lens construction via get_ov_sum() function summing top-k concept/token induction head OV matrices; (2) Word embedding extraction with optional task-specific prefixes via proj_onto_ov() function; (3) Parallelogram arithmetic testing (a-b+b'→a') via get_parallelogram_scores(); (4) Four-way comparison (raw, concept lens, token lens, all heads) with k=80 default; (5) Effective rank analysis via rank parameter sweeping across r values; (6) All 14 Word2Vec task categories implemented with results stored in cache/parallelograms/word2vec/.
Rationale.CS3_Effect_Size: Effect sizes are substantial and clearly non-trivial relative to baseline: (1) Capital Cities: concept lens 83.4% vs raw 39.3% = +44.1 percentage points, 2.12x improvement; (2) Family: concept lens 51.6% vs raw 19.2% = +32.4 pp, 2.69x improvement; (3) Present Participle: token lens 68.3% vs raw 30.1% = +38.2 pp, 2.27x improvement; (4) Past Tense: token lens 85.4% vs raw 31.9% = +53.5 pp, 2.68x improvement. Minimum absolute improvement exceeds 30 percentage points, and all relative improvements exceed 2x baseline performance.
Rationale.CS4_Justification: All key design choices and intermediate conclusions are explicitly justified: (1) k=80 heads selection justified empirically in documentation Section 6 as 'most effective' based on ablation experiments; (2) OV matrix summation approach justified by building on Elhage et al. 2021 transformer circuits framework; (3) Layer selection (20 for semantic, 16 for grammatical) justified empirically through layer sweep experiments; (4) Parallelogram arithmetic methodology justified by reference to standard Word2Vec benchmark (Mikolov et al. 2013); (5) Conclusion that concept heads copy semantic information justified causally through ablation experiments showing concept head removal damages translation but not nonsense copying.
Rationale.CS5_Statistical_Significance: Key experimental results lack appropriate uncertainty quantification: (1) No error bars or confidence intervals reported for main accuracy metrics; (2) No p-values provided for comparisons between methods (e.g., concept lens vs raw); (3) No evidence of multiple runs with different random seeds to assess variability; (4) While sample sizes are reported and substantial (n=506 for capital cities, n=480 for family), this does not substitute for proper statistical testing. Mitigating factors include large effect sizes (>30 pp) and consistency across multiple related tasks, but the absence of formal statistical significance reporting represents a methodological gap.
